title: Chhatarpur Temple
tagline: Chhatarpur Temple — Monumental Marble Shaktipith & South Ridge Heritage

heroImage.alt: Chhatarpur Temple iconic view in Delhi, India

overview.short: Shri Adhya Katyayani Shaktipith (Chhatarpur Temple) in South Delhi is India’s second-largest temple complex sprawling across 70 acres of marble shrines.
overview.description: Founded in 1974 by Sant Baba Nagpal Ji Maharaj, the Chhatarpur Temple complex is dedicated to Goddess Katyayani, the sixth aspect of Navadurga. Built entirely of lustrous Makrana marble, the sprawling 70-acre sanctum blends North and South Indian temple architecture with over 20 grand shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva, Rama, Hanuman, Ganesha, and Radha-Krishna.
overview.about: During Navratri festivals, over a hundred thousand devotees visit the sanctum daily. Located close to the Mehrauli heritage belt, the area encompasses medieval Sultanate marvels like Jahaz Mahal, Hauz-i-Shamsi, and Mehrauli Archaeological Park.

howToReach.roadNote: Located directly on Mehrauli-Gurgaon Road (MG Road) with Chhatarpur Metro Station on the Yellow Line providing direct access.

routes.byTrain: Magenta Line to Hauz Khas + Yellow Line to Chhatarpur

topPlaces.name: Shri Adhya Katyayani Shaktipith (Main Mandir)
topPlaces.description: The grand white marble sanctum of Goddess Katyayani featuring gold-plated vahanas and intricate filigree carvings.

image.alt: Shri Adhya Katyayani Shaktipith (Main Mandir) in Chhatarpur Temple, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Chhatarpur Colossal Shiva & Nandi Shrine
topPlaces.description: Monumental standing statue of Lord Shiva overlooking the main prayer square and sacred tree enclosure.

image.alt: Chhatarpur Colossal Shiva & Nandi Shrine in Chhatarpur Temple, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Jahaz Mahal (Mehrauli)
topPlaces.description: 15th-century Lodi-era Ship Palace constructed with domed pavilions reflecting gracefully on the waters of Hauz-i-Shamsi.

image.alt: Jahaz Mahal (Mehrauli) in Chhatarpur Temple, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Hauz-i-Shamsi & Jharna
topPlaces.description: Historic 13th-century water reservoir excavated by Sultan Iltutmish with surviving Mughal cascades and pleasure gardens.

image.alt: Hauz-i-Shamsi & Jharna in Chhatarpur Temple, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Mehrauli Archaeological Park
topPlaces.description: Sprawling 200-acre historic park containing over 100 medieval monuments including Jamali Kamali Mosque and Balban Tomb.

image.alt: Mehrauli Archaeological Park in Chhatarpur Temple, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Rajon ki Baoli
topPlaces.description: Magnificent 16th-century three-tiered stepwell decorated with ornate arches, pillared verandas, and stucco plasterwork.

image.alt: Rajon ki Baoli in Chhatarpur Temple, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Ahinsa Sthal (Mehrauli)
topPlaces.description: Hilltop Jain monument featuring a colossal stone idol of Lord Mahavira seated atop a scenic rocky mound on MG Road.

image.alt: Ahinsa Sthal (Mehrauli) in Chhatarpur Temple, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Zafar Mahal (Mehrauli)
topPlaces.description: The last imperial summer palace built by the Mughal dynasty under Akbar II and Bahadur Shah Zafar.

image.alt: Zafar Mahal (Mehrauli) in Chhatarpur Temple, Delhi

faq.q: What is the dress code for Chhatarpur Temple?
faq.a: Modest traditional clothing is recommended. Footwear must be deposited at the free counter before entering the sanctum.

faq.q: Which metro station connects to Chhatarpur Temple?
faq.a: Chhatarpur Metro Station on the Yellow Line is just 600 metres away from the main temple gates.

faq.q: Is Chhatarpur Temple crowded during Navratri?
faq.a: Yes, during Chaitra and Sharad Navratri the temple welcomes hundreds of thousands of pilgrims; early morning hours (6:00–8:00 AM) are best for peaceful darshan.
